plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). The dominant strategy in second-price auctions is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth if someone bids between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. With a value of $46, bidding $46 ensures I win whenever profitable and never overpay, maximizing expected profit.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid exactly my value ($17), I ensure I never overpay (since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win) and I never miss out on profitable wins (since winning at any price below $17 is profitable). Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal bid is $17.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above or below my value only risks either paying more than the item is worth or losing profitable opportunities. Bidding exactly $28 ensures I win whenever the value exceeds the competition's bids and I never overpay, maximizing expected profit.
